extracted.intended_audience: research funders, grant reviewers, university administrators, and researchers interested in equity and bias in research funding and peer review
extracted.subtask_short: assessing bias in grant peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Literature- and evidence-based overview of types of bias affecting researchers and grant/peer-review processes (disability, language, gender, sexual orientation, race, age, career stage) and published strategies to mitigate those biases. Useful for designing equitable review processes or evaluating equity in funding outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, Institutional, Age and Career Stage Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Biases arising from language of publication, institutional affiliation, age, and career stage that affect research evaluation and funding outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites work on francophone research marginalization, support to official-language minority communities, linguistic bias in reviewing, and publication/location differences; implies reviewers/funders should account for language and institutional context when assessing quality and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematic bias against women (and differential effects of gender-neutral policies) in hiring, tenure, peer review, citations, and funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes evidence and interventions: gender-neutral tenure clock effects, gendered wording in job ads, gender disparity in citations, randomized trials/interventions to reduce gender-bias habit (Carnes et al.), and systematic reviews of strategies to prevent/reduce gender bias in grant peer review (Tricco et al.). Use of these studies to design reviewer training and policy changes is implied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Based on Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (LGBTQIA+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination and microaggressions experienced by sexual and gender minority researchers that reduce participation, visibility, and funding success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References empirical reviews and reports on workplace discrimination, barriers to funding for LGBTQI+ people, nondisclosure effects on publication rates, and calls for standards in medical education — indicating reviewers/funders should consider SOGIE protections and anonymity/confidentiality issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability Bias and Accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit and implicit bias against researchers with disabilities and structural barriers in academia and grant funding (including disclosure, accommodation, and additional unpaid labour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites social vs medical models of disability, disability language guides, data on declines in grant funding for researchers with disabilities, and literature on disclosure/accommodation negotiations; implies funders should ensure accessible processes, adjust productivity expectations, and recognize disabled scholars' extra labour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias in the Peer Review Process (reliability, fairness, predictive validity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review processes can suffer from reliability, fairness, and validity problems and can reproduce bias across disciplines and funding programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References work on reliability/validity/bias/generalizability of committee peer review, commensuration bias, conservatism vs risk-taking, positive-outcome bias, and empirical studies (e.g., NIH/CIHR) showing how criterion scores relate to disparities; suggests evaluating and redesigning review instruments and procedures to improve psychometric properties and reduce bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial and Ethnic Bias / Structural Racism
rubrics_metrics.description: Race-based disparities in funding and publication (including structural racism in journals and topic-choice effects that disadvantage some racial groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites studies showing topic choice contributes to lower award rates for African American/Black scientists, analyses of structural racism in journals, and work linking criterion scores to racial disparities — indicating need for monitoring racial equity in review outcomes and potentially adjusting criteria or reviewer composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersectionality
rubrics_metrics.description: The need to analyze bias through intersecting axes (sex, gender, race, disability, language, age, career stage) rather than single-dimension approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References intersectional frameworks (e.g., for COVID-19, feminist intervention, and gender-bias frameworks) suggesting reviews and policies should adopt intersectional analyses to detect compounded disadvantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Representation and Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition of reviewer pools (e.g., under-inviting women or under-representing minority reviewers) affects fairness and diversity of evaluation outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites evidence that journals invite too few women to referee and that visible name changes and recommendation letter wording affect perceived competence; implies active steps to diversify reviewer invitations and to monitor reviewer demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic Choice and Conservatism in Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Conservatism in peer review and preferences for established topics can disadvantage novel or minority-relevant research, affecting funding equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References conservatism and risk-taking in peer review and empirical findings that topic choice contributes to award disparities; suggests designing review criteria that value innovation and topic diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive-Outcome and Publication Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency for reviewers/editors to favor positive or high-impact outcomes, which can distort evaluations of proposals and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes experimental evidence testing for positive-outcome bias; funders should be aware of such biases when using prior publication/outcome records as proxies for future potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commensuration Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias introduced when complex scholarly work is reduced to simple, commensurate metrics that may disadvantage some disciplines or researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites work on commensuration bias in peer review; implies that reliance on single metrics (e.g., number of publications, impact factors) should be balanced with qualitative assessment to avoid unfair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive Metrics of Success and Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and use broader, inclusive metrics of researcher success and impact that do not reproduce discriminatory reward systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References calls to promote inclusive metrics to dismantle discriminatory reward systems and to account for diverse contributions (teaching, community engagement, accessibility work). Funders should revise assessment frameworks accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation Strategies for Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Interventions and procedural changes to prevent or reduce bias in review processes (implicit-bias training, anonymity, reviewer guidelines, structural interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References randomized trials and systematic reviews of bias-reduction strategies (e.g., implicit-bias training, interventions to break gender-bias habit, proven workplace strategies, 17 interventions to reduce implicit racial preferences). Guidance implies implementing evidence-based interventions, monitoring effectiveness, and combining structural and individual-level approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of Sex and Gender Considerations into Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations that research proposals integrate sex and gender analysis where relevant, and funding agencies' lessons on how to require and evaluate such integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites comparative lessons from funding agencies on integrating sex and gender into biomedical research; funders/reviewers should evaluate proposals for appropriate sex/gender analysis and provide guidance to applicants.
